title: 7 Million Pairs Sold. Then Samsung Showed Up
description:
This is a made-up plan, not company news. Only step one is real: Meta and its partner EssilorLuxottica sold more than 7 million smart glasses in 2025, and on November 12, 2026 Samsung and Google opened pre-orders for their own $395 glasses, on sale December 10. Every later step is imagined by us, with no real numbers.

Sources:
- Talk Android: Samsung's Gemini-Powered Smart Glasses Open for Preorder at $395, Ship December 10 (Nov 12 2026): https://www.talkandroid.com/534903-samsung-intelligent-eyewear-smart-glasses-preorder-price/
- MIXED: Samsung's $395 smart glasses are up for preorder, but there's no display: https://mixed-news.com/en/samsung-intelligent-eyewear-preorders-december-launch/
- The Tech Outlook: Samsung's Intelligent Eyewear to be released in the US and South Korea on 10th December (Nov 13 2026): https://www.thetechoutlook.com/new-release/gadgets-release/samsungs-intelligent-eyewear-to-be-released-in-the-us-and-south-korea-on-10th-december/
- UploadVR: Meta & EssilorLuxottica Sold 7 Million Smart Glasses In 2025: https://uploadvr.com/meta-essilorluxottica-sold-7-million-smart-glasses-in-2025/

From the cited pages: EssilorLuxottica said it sold more than 7 million Ray-Ban and Oakley smart glasses (Meta partnership) in 2025, more than triple 2024 (UploadVR); Samsung announced on November 12, 2026 that its Intelligent Eyewear with Google Gemini starts at $395 in the US and goes on sale December 10, with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster frames and a camera but no display (Talk Android, MIXED, The Tech Outlook); Samsung says Gemini can help with directions and translation (MIXED). Not financial advice.

#shorts #meta #smartglasses #samsung #howtheymakemoney
loop: So next time you put on your glasses, remember:
cta: Meta or Samsung? Comment your pick.

scenes.narration: You're Meta: 7 million smart glasses sold in 2025. But on November 12, Samsung and Google opened pre-orders for their own. They start at 395 dollars and go on sale December 10.
So you decide yours must read every sign in the world. Now a tourist can read any menu on Earth. But rival glasses can translate, too. Still not enough?
So you make glasses that remember where you left your keys. Then they remember your homework and your friend's birthday.
Now everyone wants a pair. So you give one to every person on the planet.
Soon the whole world is wearing your glasses. But everyone stares at their glasses, and nobody looks up.
So your last feature is a tiny button. It turns the glasses off. You win the race by teaching the world to look up.
